findings.description: SearchableCountryDropdown, SearchableCountryWithCurrencyDropdown, SearchableCurrencySelect, and SearchableLanguageSelect share ~85% identical code (state, refs, three useEffects, handleKeyDown, select(), borderCls, dropdown shell). Extract a useSearchableDropdown hook (or generic SearchableDropdown<T> base) and have all four compose from it.

AUTOFILL_SYSTEM_PROMPT is a large prompt string embedded in gemini.ts (network layer). The resume-import prompt lives in prompt.ts with its own test file. Extract AUTOFILL_SYSTEM_PROMPT to src/resume-ai/autofillPrompt.ts to match the established pattern and enable independent testing.

AI high-confidence fills call saveLearnedMapping() directly (line 213) instead of saveElementMappings(), omitting nearbyText as a signal source and re-assembling signals manually. Replace with void saveElementMappings(domain, candidate.element, resp.profilePath) for consistency with the picker-selection path.
InfoTooltip is a reusable presentational component defined inside popup/App.tsx with no dependency on file scope. Move it to src/components/ui/InfoTooltip.tsx to enable reuse and avoid import cycles.

renderSection() is a large switch statement inlined in the component body. Extract it to a SectionRenderer component or getSectionComponent(id, props) lookup table to separate the routing concern from App layout.

SettingsSection is a 1140-line component with six distinct concerns: Appearance, AI Features, Export, Import, Cloud Backup, Reset. Consider splitting into sub-sections (AppearanceSection, AiFeaturesSection, DataManagementSection) composed in a parent Settings page.

PATH_FOCUS_TARGETS and FIELD_FOCUS_IDS are two parallel lookup tables serving the 'Go to Profile' deep-link CTA, mapping different keys to overlapping targets. As the schema grows this creates two update points. Consider a single source-of-truth record keyed by section+fieldId with derived indexes.

The fallback object in the AUTOFILL_FILL catch branch is a hardcoded zero-fill that duplicates the AutofillResult shape. If the type gains new fields the catch branch silently omits them. Import or reference an EMPTY_AUTOFILL_RESULT constant from src/autofill/index.ts.

autoprefixer is listed as a second PostCSS plugin after @tailwindcss/postcss. Tailwind CSS v4 already handles autoprefixing internally, so this is redundant. Remove autoprefixer from postcss.config.js and from package.json devDependencies.

The newEntryTick + requestAnimationFrame scroll-and-focus useEffect is duplicated verbatim across WorkHistorySection, EducationSection, LanguagesSection, SalarySection, WorkAuthorizationSection, and LinksSection — 6 identical copies. Extract a useScrollToNewEntry(ref, tick) hook.

The cls(err?) helper function (Tailwind class string for normal/error state) is copy-pasted identically in AddressSection, PersonalSection, LinksSection, WorkHistorySection, EducationSection, SalarySection, WorkAuthorizationSection, LanguagesSection, and DocumentsSection — 9 copies. Move to src/components/options/shared/fieldCls.ts and import it.

SearchableCountrySelect.filterCountries also searches by callingCode (for phone entry), while SearchableCountryDropdown only searches name and ISO. This meaningful behavioral difference is invisible from the names. Rename SearchableCountrySelect to SearchableCallingCodeSelect (or PhoneCountrySelect) to prevent future callers from choosing the wrong one.

handleSave calls saveProfile(merged) then immediately saveProfile(withDerived), two sequential writes per save. If the first write succeeds but derivation throws, the stored profile is correct but in-memory state (profile) is set to merged (without derived), creating a stale-state window. Consider computing derived fields before any storage write and only falling back if derivation fails.

detectAutoExpand() re-implements field signal extraction from a raw DOM element (querying name, id, placeholder, autocomplete, aria-label, label) instead of calling extractSignals() from signals.ts. Replace manual attribute reads with a call to extractSignals(element) to use the already-tested, maintained path.

fmtSalary() in picker.ts duplicates salary-formatting logic already in resolver.ts. Both produce "{amount} {currency}" via fmtAmount. Extract a shared formatSalaryAmount(amount, currency) helper (e.g. into utils/dateFormat.ts alongside fmtAmount) and use it in both files.

The fileChange FieldChange literal (lines 174-184) is duplicated nearly verbatim in handleRetry (lines 224-234). Extract a makeFileChange(file) helper to eliminate the duplication and prevent the two copies from diverging.

handleRetry duplicates the bulk of handleExtract's logic (abort controller setup, longWaitTimer, try/catch/finally, setChanges). The only difference is skipping the file-reading step. Refactor into a single runExtraction({ skipRead: boolean }) function that both paths call.

calculateCompletion() duplicates the validation logic already in getSectionCompletion(). The mandatory checks are written out twice in parallel. getSectionCompletion() should be called inside calculateCompletion() and the section booleans used to drive the check() calls.
check() and optCheck() are identically structured inner functions differing only in their target array. Extract a makeChecker(target) factory and call it twice to remove the structural duplication.

validateImportedProfile() rejects salary.current.amount of 0 (cur.amount > 0), but profileCompletion.ts accepts 0 as valid (amount >= 0). This inconsistency means a profile with amount=0 will fail re-import validation. The import validator should use cur.amount >= 0.

stripMarkdown is defined in gemini.ts (network layer) but is a pure text utility with no Gemini-specific logic. It should live in a shared utility module so it can be reused without importing from the network-layer file.

AIOptionPayload, AIFieldPayload, and AIFieldResponse are declared inside gemini.ts (network layer) but describe the autofill domain model. Move them to src/resume-ai/types.ts alongside FieldChange, ImportError, etc. to keep type declarations co-located.

professional.summary field def uses section: 'Work History' (line 172) and professional.noticePeriod uses the same (line 184). Both belong under a 'Professional' section heading in the diff UI, not 'Work History'. This mislabeling causes confusing grouping in the import review screen.

The 'Missing' dropdown trigger and panel are duplicated for the !isCoreComplete case and the isCoreComplete && optionalFieldsRemaining > 0 case. The only differences are panel heading text and dot color. Extract a MissingDropdown sub-component with those as props.

The optional prop is accepted but silently ignored — its JSDoc says 'the Optional tag is no longer rendered'. Remove the prop from the interface and update all callers that still pass optional. Dead prop creates confusion about whether it controls rendering.

Notice period validation logic (error message with pluralised unit) is inlined in the onChange handler for the value input, the onChange handler for the unit selector, and the validate() function — 3 separate copies. Extract a validateNoticeValue(value, unit) helper.

The load function inside the Drive state useEffect is wrapped in a named function then immediately called, and also assigned as handler. Just define handler once and call it directly — the intermediate load alias is noise.

handleImportReviewSave is a one-liner that just calls performImportSave. Since performImportSave already has the required signature, pass it directly to ImportReviewScreen's onSave prop and remove the wrapper.
handleGoToApiKey duplicates the body of the target === 'gemini-api-key' branch in applyFocusTarget (lines 112-115). Extract a shared focusGeminiKey() helper called by both.

handleNavigate is a one-liner wrapper around setActiveSection with a redundant cast. Accept SectionId directly in CompletionBanner and Sidebar prop types, or inline the cast at the call site, and remove handleNavigate.

sendToActiveTab is a regular async function inside the component recreated on every render. Wrap in useCallback with an empty dependency array so it isn't re-created and can safely be listed as a dependency in any future useEffect.

handleConfirmFill duplicates the fill-dispatch and result-handling logic from the 'nothing pre-filled' branch of handleAutofill (lines 156-163). Extract a shared dispatchFill(mode) helper that both branches call.

_learnedMappings is fetched with getLearnedMappings() inside executeAutofill() but never used (prefixed with _ and immediately discarded). This is a dead storage read on every autofill execution. Remove both the await call and the binding.

GEMINI_MODEL_PRIORITY includes 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite' and 'gemini-3.5-flash' but the comment says 'gemini-2.5-flash-lite' is a valid stored model NOT a probe candidate. If gemini-3.x models are also stored-only models, the comment is incomplete; if they are valid probe targets the comment is misleading. Document the relationship clearly.

getThemePreference() only checks 'light' and 'dark' explicitly, falling through to 'system' for everything else. 'system' stored explicitly is accepted via fallback implicitly. Add an explicit 'system' check to make the intent clear and prevent confusion if the type is extended.

font-weight: 650 and font-weight: 750 (lines 150, 237, 328) are not valid CSS font-weight values. Browsers round these to nearest valid values (600 and 800). Replace with standard values (600/700 or 700/800) to make intent explicit.

Two consecutive if(match.fieldPath) guards at lines 422 and 425 in the noData branch check the same condition independently. Merge into a single if block that pushes to both noDataFields and aiTextCandidates.
runAutofill() is exported as 'legacy single-phase entry point' but has zero callers outside this file. Remove it or add @deprecated JSDoc and document where it should be called from.

The resolve() private wrapper is a one-liner that only converts empty string from resolveProfileValue to null. Inline resolveProfileValue(profile, fieldPath) || null at each call site and remove the wrapper.

The setTimeout + document.addEventListener pattern for activeOutsideHandler registration is duplicated in both showNoDataCta() and showPicker(). Extract a registerOutsideHandler(handler) helper so the timing behaviour cannot diverge.
isVisibleInput() is a one-line wrapper that simply delegates to isElementVisible() with no additional logic. Remove it and call isElementVisible directly at its two call sites.

findBestOption() uses toLowerCase().trim() for matching instead of the project's canonical normalize() function from normalizer.ts. This is inconsistent and could miss options differing only in punctuation or hyphens. Replace with normalize() calls.

CONF_AI_YELLOW and CONF_CONTEXT both have value 0.70 and represent structurally different concepts. The comment correctly notes they 'can drift'. Add an explicit '// NOTE: intentionally equal today but conceptually separate' remark to make the duplication explicit.

The setValue helpers on every FieldDef entry repeat the same spread pattern ~20 times: { ...p, personal: { ...(p.personal ?? {} as Profile['personal']), field: v } }. A small patchNested(p, 'personal', { firstName: v }) helper would eliminate repetition and the forced casts.

GeminiModel includes 'gemini-3.5-flash' and 'gemini-3.1-flash-lite' which don't match any known Gemini naming convention (real models are gemini-2.5-flash, gemini-2.5-pro). If these are future placeholders comment them as such; if they are typos they are dead enum values that will fail at runtime.

COUNTRIES.sort() is called as a side effect at module load time, mutating the exported array after the popular-countries-pinned ordering is defined. The comment 'Popular countries pinned first' is misleading — the sort silently erases the pin order on load. Document whether alphabetical or pinned order is the intent.
VALID_VETERAN is reused for disabilityStatus validation. Rename to VALID_YES_NO_PNTS or introduce a separate VALID_DISABILITY constant with the same values so the intent is self-documenting.

Multipart boundary is generated with Date.now() + Math.random().toString(36). crypto.randomUUID() (already used in storage.ts for profile IDs) would be more robust and is consistent with how randomness is handled elsewhere.
merged.push([...current] as [number, number]) spreads an already-typed tuple unnecessarily. Push current directly to remove noise without any safety trade-off.

The GET_STATUS IIFE in the second useEffect has no cleanup guard. If the popup unmounts before the promise resolves, the state setter fires on an unmounted component. Add a cancelled flag or AbortController guard.

The jb:ai:nudge:dismissed session-storage read and getGeminiApiKey fetch are in two separate useEffect hooks that both run once on mount with no dependencies. Combining them into a single effect or Promise.all reduces async round-trips during popup initialization.

The 'No AI key' tooltip in the Autofill section header uses raw group/group-hover Tailwind classes instead of the InfoTooltip component defined in the same file. Refactor to use InfoTooltip for consistency.

sectionProps is reconstructed as a new object literal { profile, onSave: handleSave } on every render, causing every section component to receive a new prop reference even when profile and handleSave haven't changed. Wrap in useMemo.

The settings case in renderSection passes an inline arrow () => handleImportComplete(...) to onResetComplete, creating a new function reference every render. Extract it to a named handler (handleResetComplete) for stability.
_geminiModel (underscore prefix) is set and read in the debounce callback. The underscore suggests unused but it is actively read. Rename to geminiModel or activeGeminiModel for clarity.

DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL is hardcoded locally in SettingsSection. If this value is also defined in src/utils/storage.ts or src/resume-ai/gemini.ts, import from there rather than duplicating, to prevent drift when the model name changes.

The Work Arrangement radio group uses onChange={() => {}} as a no-op plus onClick for toggle logic. This is an accessibility anti-pattern: screen readers won't announce the radio as interactive. Use onChange for value change and track deselect separately.
checked={row.isCurrent ?? false} is redundant — isCurrent is guaranteed non-null by initRow (defaults to false) and emptyRow. Remove the ?? false.
isValidYear is defined inside the component body but doesn't close over any state. Hoist it to module scope to avoid re-creation on every render.

MONTHS in DateOfBirthPicker uses value: number (1-12) while MONTHS in MonthYearPicker uses value: string ('01'-'12'). Both contain the same 12 labels. Consider a shared MONTH_NAMES constant to prevent label drift.

normalizeExtractedProfile does two sequential spread-copy passes over the result (lines 108-114 for workHistory, lines 116-124 for professional.summary). These could be combined into a single object construction, reducing allocations.
fillDemoData() and clearDemoData() access form.elements without null-checking form first. If the element ID changes, both throw. Add if (!form) return; at the top of both functions.

The index % 7 === 0 heuristic to assign the 'review' CSS class has no comment explaining the intent (~14% yellow/review-state). Extract as a named constant or add a comment so future maintainers understand it is intentional.

globals.node is included for all TypeScript files. Extension source files run in the browser or service worker, not Node.js. Having Node globals active means ESLint won't flag accidental Node API usage in content scripts or popup code. Scope Node globals to config/build files only.

filterCountries(search) runs on every render and re-scans the full COUNTRIES array (200+ entries) synchronously. Wrap in useMemo(() => filterCountries(search), [search]). Same applies to SearchableCountryWithCurrencyDropdown, SearchableCurrencySelect, and SearchableLanguageSelect.

dictionaryExact() iterates all FIELD_DICTIONARY entries on every call. Since the dictionary is static, build a reverse-lookup Map<string, string> (term → fieldPath) once at module load. Reduces inner-loop cost from O(entries × variations) to O(1) per lookup.
calculateCompletion(profile) and getSectionCompletion(profile) are called unconditionally on every render, traversing the entire profile object. Wrap both in useMemo with profile as the dependency.

In check() inner function, groups.find((x) => x.sectionId === sectionId) performs a linear scan per failing check. With 15 checks this is negligible, but a Map<string, CompletionGroup> keyed by sectionId would be O(1). Same pattern in optCheck.

scanFields() calls getComputedStyle(el) and getBoundingClientRect() on every element during filter pass. Both force style recalculation/layout. Reorder checks: hidden attribute and disabled first (zero cost), then offsetParent, then getComputedStyle, then getBoundingClientRect only as last resort.

applyChanges calls FIELD_DEFS.find(d => d.id === change.id) inside a loop over changes — O(n²). Pre-build a Map<string, FieldDef> from FIELD_DEFS at module level (it's immutable) to make lookups O(1).
sectionsWithOptionalGaps and sectionFullCompletion are derived values rebuilt on every render. Combine into the same useMemo block as calculateCompletion/getSectionCompletion.

The color/colorMap derivation (lines 202-207) runs on every render even when percentage hasn't changed. Move into a useMemo or pure helper function to avoid re-creating the object on unrelated re-renders.
aiByFieldId is built with new Map(...) on every render. Wrap in useMemo with session.ai as the dependency.

runAIAutofill has no tests. Critical untested paths: high-confidence fills decrement lowConfidence/noData and increment noReview; low-confidence fills add a picker entry; aiGreenFilled set is populated for green fills; radio and checkbox fill paths; graceful return true when AI call throws.

No tests exist for any section component's validate() logic (e.g., WorkHistorySection's end-date-before-start-date check, EducationSection's year range boundary, PersonalSection's email regex). These are the highest-impact validation paths — a bug here silently stores corrupt data.

resolveFieldsWithAI and parseAutofillResponse have no test coverage. parseAutofillResponse is the critical boundary where AI output becomes trusted data. Missing: non-JSON returns [], invalid items filtered, items missing fieldId rejected, items with unexpected confidence rejected.

checkApiKey and validateApiKey have no test coverage. validateApiKey has non-trivial logic: iterates model priority list, distinguishes auth failures (401/403) from model-specific failures (404, 400 with non-key message). The 400-body-parse branch is especially hard to verify without tests.

The two-phase autofill flow (scan → confirming → fill with mode) is the primary user-facing interaction path with no unit or integration tests. Add tests for: (1) scan returning preFilledCount > 0 → confirming state, (2) merge dispatch, (3) overwrite dispatch, (4) error state on rejection.

retryPendingDriveSync has no tests. Its conditional logic (pendingSync flag, token presence, profile null-check) is testable with mocked storage and driveSync. Add: (1) no retry when pendingSync false, (2) no retry when token missing, (3) sync called when both present.

connectDrive() is not tested at all. Non-trivial branching: OAuth failure path, successful OAuth + Drive lookup failure path (writes pendingSync:true), full success path. Missing the 'connection succeeded but file lookup failed' branch.
saveLearnedMapping() has no test confirming behavior when chrome.storage.local.set fails (the rejected Promise propagation). The read-modify-write loop failure path is uncovered.

Layer 3 (fuzzy) test only asserts confidence > 0. Add two tests: one for strong fuzzy match (score > CONF_FUZZY_THRESHOLD) verifying confidence = score * CONF_FUZZY_STRONG_MULT, one for weak fuzzy match verifying CONF_FUZZY_WEAK_MULT.

fillFileField has no tests. It handles base64 decoding, MIME type parsing, DataTransfer reconstruction, and event dispatch — all with silent fallbacks. Add tests for: successful reconstruction dispatching input and change events; malformed data-URL prefix returns false; missing comma in base64 returns false.

clearHighlights() tests do not verify that data attributes (jbOrigBackground, jbOrigTransition) are removed from elements after clearing — only that background color is restored. Add assertions that confirm el.dataset.jbOrigBackground and el.dataset.jbOrigTransition are undefined after clearHighlights().

prompt.test.ts only checks surface-level string presence. It does not verify the emitted schema matches the Profile type (e.g., salary.current.country present, coverLetter absent per exclusion rule, education date rules stated). A schema-structure test would catch prompt/Profile drift earlier.

applyChanges with array-typed fields (workHistory, education, languages, workAuthorization, salary.expected) is not tested. Missing: verify accepting a workHistory conflict replaces the whole array, declining it leaves it intact.

Test environment is set to 'node' but the project tests DOM interactions (autofill, field scanning, filler, signals). jsdom and @types/jsdom are already installed. Switching to environment: 'jsdom' and adding a setupFiles entry for Chrome API stubs would make the test environment consistent.

The professional section of validateImportedProfile() (lines 120-128) is a pass-through with no structural validation of noticePeriod shape. Zero tests for importing a profile with professional.summary or professional.noticePeriod. Add tests for pass-through and verify non-object noticePeriod is excluded.
overwriteDriveWithLocal() is not tested at all. A simple test verifying it delegates to syncProfileToDrive and propagates the result would improve coverage.

revokeDriveToken() is not tested for the silent-failure path. The catch block at driveSync.ts:73 swallows network errors silently — add a test that confirms the error is swallowed and the function still resolves.
clearAllStorage() test verifies profile and learnedMappings are cleared but never tests that applicationHistory is also removed, even though it is in the storageRemove call.

resolvePathFocusTarget() is exported but has zero test coverage. The longest-prefix match loop (segments.pop() loop) is untested — a path like 'salary.expected.0.currency' should resolve to 'salary' via prefix walk.
formatISODate() is exported but completely untested. It performs local-calendar date formatting which differs from UTC-based toISOString(); the local-vs-UTC corner case is unverified.

The theme.test.ts beforeEach calls applyTheme('system') to reset state, which invokes matchMedia. If stubMatchMedia has not been called yet (first test in 'applyTheme(dark)' group), the call may hit the real jsdom matchMedia. Consider resetting via applyTheme('light') which never touches matchMedia.

scanRadioGroups() and scanCheckboxGroups() are not tested at all. Key behaviours to cover: groups with fewer than 2 options filtered for radio; consent checkboxes flagged by isConsent; anonymous checkboxes get synthetic keys; getGroupLegend returns fieldset legend.

workHistory.N.description and education.N.description fall through to the generic traversal path with no test. Add one test each to guard against a future accidental special-case breaking plain string sub-fields.
saveSection.test.ts doesn't test the optional duration parameter being forwarded to showToast. The third parameter could be silently dropped and tests would still pass.

No tests for the display function for any complex field (phone, noticePeriod, salary, workHistory, education). Display functions contain logic (replace, pluralisation, date formatting) that can silently break.
normalizeExtractedProfile tests don't cover workHistory and professional.summary present simultaneously. The current suite tests them in isolation only.
coverLetter pass-through in the documents section (profileValidator.ts line 320) is entirely untested — no test imports a profile with a documents.coverLetter field.

The lint script uses --ext .ts,.tsx which is an ESLint v8 flag. ESLint v9 flat config ignores --ext entirely — file targeting is done via the files glob in eslint.config.js. Remove --ext .ts,.tsx from both lint and lint:fix scripts.
autoprefixer is listed as a devDependency but Tailwind CSS v4 bundles its own vendor-prefix handling. Remove autoprefixer from package.json (already covered by f-0009 in architecture).

The @ alias is resolved to the project root (.) in vitest.config.ts. WXT already configures @ to src/ via its Vite/Vitest integration. Consider importing from wxt/testing instead of vitest/config to inherit WXT's alias and module stubs, avoiding drift between build-time and test-time resolution.
entrypoints/popup/App.css contains only a comment and is never imported anywhere (only style.css is imported in main.tsx). This file is dead — remove it.

SearchableCountrySelect imports findCountry from countries.ts; the other three Searchable components inline COUNTRIES.find() directly. Minor inconsistency — standardize on findCountry across all four for clarity.

Zero test coverage for the entire picker module: buildPickerTree, live search/filter, expand/collapse state, theme switching, and the noData CTA. Largest and most stateful file in the autofill folder with no picker.test.ts at all.

Missing coverage for the silent re-fill flow (runSilentRefill) and edit-watcher blur-based promotion of manually-filled fields (attachEditWatchers, visibility listener) — the most stateful, order-sensitive logic in the file, completely unexercised by index.test.ts.
ai.ts reimplements bestLabel()'s fallback chain inline (label||ariaLabel||placeholder||name) instead of calling the bestLabel() helper it already imports and uses elsewhere in the same file.

scanFields() re-implements the same disabled/hidden/aria-hidden/offsetParent/display/visibility/opacity/zero-rect checks as isElementVisible() nearly verbatim instead of calling it (plus its own extra readOnly check).

fillSelect() and findBestAriaOption() implement the identical 3-tier matching strategy (exact value/text, normalized value/text, fuzzy >= threshold) separately for native <option> vs ARIA option elements, ~70 lines of logic hand-kept in sync.

dictionaryFuzzy() does a full linear scan of ~100+ dictionary terms per normalized signal, up to 5x per field across Layers 3 and 4 combined, with no memoization — unlike dictionaryExact() which was explicitly optimized into an O(1) Map lookup.

MutableResult hand-duplicates fields already declared on AutofillResult (noReview/needReview/lowConfidence/noData) instead of deriving via Pick<>, so a rename on the source type won't be caught by the compiler here.

useSearchableDropdown unified the state logic across the 5 searchable-dropdown components, but the surrounding rendering (trigger button shell, panel wrapper, search input, listbox with highlight classes, empty state) is still copy-pasted ~40-60 lines each across SearchableCallingCodeSelect, SearchableCountryDropdown, SearchableCountryWithCurrencyDropdown, SearchableCurrencySelect, and SearchableLanguageSelect.
DocumentsSection's urlCls is a hand-written ternary producing the exact same two class strings as the shared fieldCls() helper, but the file never imports it.

MonthYearPicker and DateOfBirthPicker each independently reinvent the same border/ring/bg/text field-styling classes instead of reusing the shared fieldCls() helper; MonthYearPicker also layers on a disabledCls the shared helper doesn't support yet.

Save-button markup (identical className string, only label/disabled differ) is duplicated verbatim across ~9 section components, plus two more Add-Entry-button style variants each duplicated across 3 files — no shared SaveButton/AddEntryButton despite the established FormField/RemoveButton/ExpandableCard pattern.
Zero test coverage for useSearchableDropdown's keyboard navigation (ArrowUp/Down clamping, Enter-to-select, Escape-to-close, outside-click-to-close), used by all 5 searchable dropdown components.
Zero test coverage for DateOfBirthPicker's pure functions (daysInMonth, computePartial, buildDOB) — real edge cases including Feb 29 leap-year handling and day auto-clamping when month/year changes.

The identical complex optional-chain response-text extraction ((data as {...})?.candidates?.[0]?.content?.parts?.[0]?.text) is copy-pasted verbatim in both extractFromResume and resolveFieldsWithAI instead of a shared extractGeminiText() helper.

salary.current's diff display (displayCurrent/displaySuggested) never includes the optional country field, unlike salary.expected which does append it — a reviewer can't see a country-only change during a Resume Import or Drive Restore conflict.

FIELD_DEFS display-function tests have zero coverage for professional.summary (including its 120-char truncation boundary), links.linkedin/portfolio/custom, workAuthorization, languages, and documents.cv.url/file's bespoke doubly-nested setValue logic.
extractFromResume and resolveFieldsWithAI type their model parameter as bare string instead of the GeminiModel union, losing compile-time protection against a typo'd or stale model id.

The AI-autofill prompt is assembled inline in resolveFieldsWithAI instead of exposing an equivalent buildAutofillPrompt() in autofillPrompt.ts, unlike resume extraction which cleanly separates prompt construction into buildPrompt() in prompt.ts.
The doc comment describing findCountryByNameOrCode's backward-compat behavior is misplaced above COUNTRIES.sort()/Object.freeze(COUNTRIES) instead of above the function it actually documents.

normalizeBullets' top-level doc comment lists covered bullet markers but omits two (▹ and ■) that are actually handled by BULLET_RE and correctly listed in a second, more detailed comment further down. Cosmetic doc drift.

session.scanner.find(s => s.fieldId === m.fieldId) runs inside session.mapping.map(...), an O(n*m) linear scan per row, when the same file already builds aiByFieldId as a useMemo'd Map for the identical fieldId-lookup shape 15 lines earlier.

chrome.storage.session is accessed directly and inconsistently across popup/App.tsx, options/App.tsx, and background.ts, each with its own inline try/catch, with no equivalent wrapper module to chrome.storage.local's storage.ts.
AutofillScanResult.totalMatched is declared but never read anywhere; handleAutofill only checks scan?.preFilledCount. Dead field on an otherwise-small interface.

documents.coverLetter is passed through wholesale with zero field-level validation, while documents.cv immediately above is deeply validated (url length cap, file shape with name/size/base64 typechecks) in the same function.

links.custom is accepted with only an Array.isArray check and cast straight through, unlike every other array field in the same function (workAuthorization, workHistory, education, languages) which validates each entry's shape and drops/reports invalid ones.

downloadBackupFromDrive's corrupted/partial-backup fallback paths (non-object JSON, missing .profile, JSON parse throw) are never exercised by driveSync.test.ts, which only covers full success and an HTTP-status lookup failure.

The OPEN_OPTIONS handler (focus-path payload shape, chrome.storage.session write, openOptionsPage call) is inline inside defineBackground(). Per this project's own documented WXT trap, test files can't live under entrypoints/, so this logic structurally cannot get test coverage without extraction to a src/ helper.

The clearAllStorage test seeds applicationHistory with an object shaped {id, company, position, appliedAt, url} cast via 'as unknown as ApplicationEntry[]', but the real ApplicationEntry type requires jobTitle/status, not company/position — the cast silences a real type mismatch and the test gives no signal about correct usage.

@types/jsdom is an unused devDependency — a full-codebase grep for JSDOM finds zero hits. DOM tests use the // @vitest-environment jsdom pragma, which only needs the jsdom package itself, not its type stubs.

No .prettierignore exists anywhere in the repo. pnpm format runs prettier --write . unscoped and is willing to reformat demo-apply-form/** and docs/**, which eslint.config.js explicitly excludes from linting — the two formatting/lint tools disagree about whether these hand-authored static sites are in scope.

The 'Back to Job Buddy' link uses a relative './' path while the two tags in the same file correctly use the absolute /job-buddy/assets/icons/icon.svg path (necessary since a GitHub Pages 404 can be served from any arbitrarily deep broken URL). On a deep broken link the relative './' resolves to the wrong subdirectory while the images still load.

Brand colors #4B79F7 (blue) and #0D1B3E (navy) are independently hardcoded in three unrelated files — docs/index.html, docs/project-site/assets/style.css, and demo-apply-form/assets/css/styles.css — with no shared source. A rebrand requires manually touching all three with nothing to catch a missed spot.

The page hardcodes a stale version (v1.9.1, vs actual package.json version 1.10.0) and a stale commit hash (8f4458e5, several releases behind current HEAD), despite branding itself as 'generated from repository evidence' at a specific commit — implying it should be periodically regenerated.

Tailwind is loaded via the runtime CDN script (<script src="https://cdn.tailwindcss.com">), un-deferred, blocking HTML parsing while it downloads and then runs a full JIT compiler client-side on every load of the site's primary marketing/conversion page. Tailwind's own docs state the CDN build isn't meant for production.

All six screenshot tags (~40-124KB webp each, ~370KB combined) load eagerly with no loading="lazy" and no explicit width/height, unlike the two icon tags which set both — below-the-fold images load immediately regardless of scroll position and missing dimensions invite layout shift.

Google Fonts is loaded via a CSS @import at the top of the stylesheet instead of an HTML <link> — a known render-blocking anti-pattern (the browser must fetch and parse the parent stylesheet before it even discovers the import). docs/index.html already does this correctly via <link rel="preconnect"> + <link rel="stylesheet">.

The applicationForm submit listener has no null-check, unlike fillDemoData(), clearDemoData(), and the resetButton listener earlier in the same small file, all of which guard against a missing element.

handleGeminiKeyChange only guards the background model-probe step (probeIdRef, line 205) against overlapping debounce cycles. The earlier checkApiKey/saveGeminiApiKey/saveGeminiModel(DEFAULT) steps (lines 186-201) have no such guard. If the user clears the key field (line 174, which synchronously calls clearGeminiSettings()) while a previous debounce callback is still awaiting checkApiKey/saveGeminiApiKey, that stale callback can complete afterward and re-save the very key the user just cleared. Extend the same id-guard pattern used for the probe to the validate+save steps.

`_geminiModel` state is write-only: `setGeminiModel` is called at lines 153, 200, 211 and 216, but the state value itself is never read anywhere in the component (not rendered, not passed down). Either remove the state entirely or replace it with a plain variable/ref, since every `setGeminiModel` call currently forces a needless re-render for a value nothing consumes.

handleFileChange's empty-profile fast path (lines 299-320) re-implements the same save+merge+toast+callback sequence as performImportSave (lines 333-363: saveProfile, merge learnedMappings, saveApplicationHistory, skipped-fields toast, onImportComplete) instead of reusing it. Extract the common logic into one shared helper both call, so the two import code paths can't drift apart.

handleFileChange (line 299, via calculateCompletion) and handleDriveConnect (line 386, via calculateCompletion) each independently compute 'is the current profile empty enough to skip the merge/review flow' to decide between a direct save and a diff+summary/review flow. Extract a shared `isProfileEmpty(profile)` helper used by both instead of duplicating the completion-percentage check and the branching shape.

geminiDebounceRef's pending setTimeout is only cleared when the input changes again (line 172) — there is no unmount cleanup. If the user navigates away from Settings while the 800ms debounce is pending, the timeout still fires later and calls setState (setGeminiKeyStatus etc.) on an unmounted component. Add a useEffect that clears the timer on unmount, mirroring the pattern already used for abortControllerRef/longWaitTimerRef in ResumeImportSection.tsx.

The primary-button and secondary-button Tailwind class strings are duplicated verbatim roughly 8-10 times across this file (e.g. lines 658, 708, 732, 766, 804, 989, 1069, 1119). Given `fieldCls.ts` already establishes the precedent of centralizing shared class strings, extract equivalent `btnPrimaryCls`/`btnSecondaryCls` constants.

Icon-only dialog close buttons (the × glyph) at lines ~913, 1020 and 1092 have no `aria-label`, so a screen reader announces only "×" with no indication it closes the dialog. Add `aria-label="Close"` to each.
The dialog close button (the × glyph, ~line 306) has no `aria-label`, same issue as SettingsSection.tsx's dialog close buttons. Add `aria-label="Close"`.

The drag/drop upload zone is a plain `<div onClick={...}>` (lines 334-343) with no `role="button"`, `tabIndex`, or keydown handler, so it can't be reached or activated with a keyboard alone. Add `role="button" tabIndex={0}` plus an Enter/Space `onKeyDown` handler, or wrap the hidden file `<input>` in a `<label>` instead of relying on the div's onClick.

`PROGRESS_STEPS.findIndex(...)` is recomputed inside the `.map()` callback on every rendered step (3x per render) instead of once above the `.map()`. Hoist `const currentIdx = PROGRESS_STEPS.findIndex(s => s.id === progressStep);` above the `.map()` call.

handleExtract (lines 187-215) and handleRetry (lines 219-234) duplicate the same setup block — new AbortController, clear errorMsg/errorCode, reset showLongWait, start longWaitTimerRef — before diverging. Extract the shared setup into one helper both call.

`resolvesEmpty()` (called per signal row during render, line 117) and the `domains`/per-domain `signals` sorts (lines 233, 258) run unmemoized on every render of the section. Since a re-render happens on every persist() and on every chrome.storage.onChanged event, wrap these in useMemo keyed on `mappings`/`profile` to avoid re-sorting and re-resolving every row each time.

The entire Google Drive connect/restore/conflict flow (handleDriveConnect, handleRestoreFromDrive's 'empty' case, handleKeepLocal, handleDriveReviewSave) has zero test coverage, even though it implements the same 'merge, never overwrite, learned mappings' safety invariant that IS tested for the plain JSON import path. Add an equivalent test that drives connectDrive() returning a backup and asserts the merge behavior on restore.
handleExport (JSON blob construction, filename, and the 'No profile data to export' warning when getProfile() resolves null) is not exercised by any test.

No test covers the `errorCode === 'rate_limit'` branch (distinct copy + link to Google AI Studio), the final 'done' screen (summary counts/pluralization), or performSave's catch branch (onSave rejecting → 'Save failed. Please try again.' toast).

The `chrome.storage.onChanged` listener (component lines 184-195), which the component's own comment calls out as important for staying in sync with background autofill-learning writes, is never exercised. The `persist()` failure toast and the initial-load failure toast (Promise.all rejecting) are also untested.

The Work Arrangement radio inputs use a no-op `onChange={() => {}}` and drive the actual state change from `onClick` (to allow deselecting a selected radio). Native keyboard navigation between radio buttons in the same named group fires a `change` event, not a `click` event, so arrow-key users can visually move the browser's radio selection without the no-op `onChange` ever updating React state — the saved value can silently diverge from what's shown. Move the toggle-to-deselect logic into `onChange` (checking `e.target.checked`) instead of `onClick`.

`handleYearChange` (lines 134-149) and `handleDateBlur` (lines 153-199) are near-duplicates of the same-named functions in EducationSection.tsx (lines 76-145) — same algorithm, only the min/max year constants and the YYYY-vs-YYYY-MM end/start normalization differ. Worth extracting into a shared `useDateRangeValidation(minYear, maxYear, { monthOptional })` hook to avoid maintaining two copies of the same validation state machine.

`calculateExperience(entries as unknown as WorkHistoryEntry[])` runs unmemoized on every render, including renders triggered by unrelated field edits. For profiles with many work entries this recomputes date-parsing work on every keystroke. Wrap in `useMemo` keyed on the entries' `startDate`/`isCurrent`/`endDate` fields.

`validate()` includes `if (!currentPeriod) e.currentPeriod = 'Period is required';` but `currentPeriod` is a `<select>` with only 'monthly'/'annual' options and no blank option, initialized to `'monthly'` — it can never be empty, so this branch is dead code. Remove it (or add a blank option if an unset state is actually intended).

The 'Enter a valid amount' branch (negative or NaN current/expected salary amount) in `validate()` and the live `onChange` handler is never tested — only the 'amount required' and country/currency-migration paths are covered.

`handleFile` (used by both the file-picker input and `handleDrop`) only checks `file.size` against `MAX_FILE_SIZE`; it never checks the file extension/MIME type against the advertised 'PDF, DOCX' restriction. The `accept=".pdf,.doc,.docx"` attribute on the hidden `<input type="file">` is bypassed entirely by drag-and-drop, so any file type can be uploaded and stored as base64 in the profile despite the UI's stated restriction. Add an extension/type check in `handleFile`.

`MAX_FILE_SIZE` rejection (the 'File exceeds 4 MB limit' `sizeError` path in `DocUploader.handleFile`) has no test at all, despite CLAUDE.md calling out the 4 MB cap as an explicit domain rule. Add a test that uploads/drops an oversized `File` and asserts the size error renders and save is blocked appropriately.

`id={key === 'linkedin' ? 'field-linkedin' : key === 'portfolio' ? 'field-portfolio' : undefined}` is a nested ternary that just reconstructs `field-${key}` the hard way. Simplify to `id={`field-${key}`}`.

`Row.proficiency` is typed as the non-nullable `LanguageProficiency`, but `emptyRow()` assigns `'' as LanguageProficiency` — a cast that lies to the type system. `WorkAuthorizationSection.tsx`'s analogous `LocalRow` correctly types the field as `WorkAuthorizationStatus | ''`. Type `Row.proficiency` as `LanguageProficiency | ''` here too so the empty/unselected state is representable without an unsafe cast.

No test exercises the Work Arrangement radio group (onsite/remote/hybrid, including the click-to-deselect behavior) or the Notice Period value validation (min 1, per-unit max, non-numeric input) when 'Available Later' is selected.

No test covers the email-format branch of `fieldError`/`validate` (malformed email) or the Date of Birth year-range branches ('Date of birth cannot be after <year>' / 'Year must be <year> or later'). Only the 'empty/required' and partial-DOB paths are tested.

Unlike WorkHistorySection.test.tsx's equivalent coverage, this file never exercises the live year-range validation path (`handleYearChange`/`onYearChange`) using `EDU_MIN_YEAR`/`EDU_MAX_YEAR`, so a regression that swapped in the wrong bounds for Education specifically would go undetected here.

Internal `month`/`yearStr` state is seeded from the `value` prop only in the `useState` initializer, with no `useEffect` to resync when `value` changes on an already-mounted instance. WorkHistorySection.tsx and EducationSection.tsx render one `MonthYearPicker` per entry keyed by index and delete via `rows.filter((_, i) => i !== idx)`; deleting a non-last entry shifts every later index, so React reuses the same picker instances while their `value` prop now refers to a different entry's date. The displayed month/year stays stale until the user retypes it, and if they edit it, `emit()` computes from the stale local state and can write a wrong date back onto the wrong row. Fix: add a `useEffect(() => { setMonth(...); setYearStr(...); }, [value])` to resync, or key the list items by a stable entry id instead of index.

Same pattern as MonthYearPicker: `month`/`day`/`year`/`dayStr`/`yearStr` are derived from `value` only via the `useState` initializer, never resynced on later prop changes. Currently dormant since PersonalSection only renders one instance, but worth the same `useEffect` resync fix for defense-in-depth.

The `<label>` has no `htmlFor` and does not wrap `children`, so it is never programmatically associated with the input it labels — clicking the label text won't focus/activate the field in any browser, and screen readers won't announce the label when the input receives focus. Every section in the app funnels through this component (9 sections), so this is a systemic accessibility gap. Fix: accept an `id` prop and set `htmlFor={id}` on the label, or wrap `children` inside the `<label>` element.

Reimplements the open/search/highlight state machinery that already exists in `useSearchableDropdown`, instead of composing from it like the other four Searchable* components do. The item-rendering here is genuinely different (grouped tree vs flat list) so full reuse isn't drop-in, but the open/search/outside-click plumbing (~40 lines) could still be extracted and shared.

The search `<input>` and the `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` rows implement the ARIA listbox pattern but have no `onKeyDown` handler at all — no arrow-key highlight, no Enter-to-select, no Escape-to-close. A keyboard-only user can open the panel but cannot select an option without clicking it.

`confirmDelete` has no escape hatch: clicking the summary/expand toggle, clicking anywhere outside the card, or pressing Escape does not reset it. A user who clicks the remove icon and then changes their mind by clicking elsewhere leaves the card silently armed. Add an outside-click or blur handler that resets `confirmDelete` to false.

The chevron toggle button (▲/▼) and the summary button that also toggles expand/collapse have no `aria-expanded` attribute, and the chevron button has no accessible name. Add `aria-expanded={expanded}` and an `aria-label` (e.g. "Expand"/"Collapse") to the chevron button.

The `<button>` has no `type="button"` (defaults to `type="submit"`), unlike every other button in this directory. Currently harmless since no section wraps its fields in a native `<form>`, but it's a landmine if one ever is added.

MonthYearPicker's `MONTHS` array (zero-padded string values) and DateOfBirthPicker's `MONTHS` array (numeric values) duplicate the same 12 month labels in two incompatible value shapes. Could share one canonical list with a formatter at each call site.

No dedicated test file exists for SearchableCountryDropdown, SearchableCountryWithCurrencyDropdown, SearchableCurrencySelect, or SearchableLanguageSelect. Component-specific behavior is consequently unverified: SearchableCountryWithCurrencyDropdown's `currencyFor` lookup/fallback and currency-text search match, and SearchableLanguageSelect's legacy free-text `displayName` fallback when `value` doesn't resolve to a known language code.

`parseDOB` (exported from dateOfBirthMath.ts) has no direct unit test — only `daysInMonth`, `computePartial`, and `buildDOB` are tested. It's exercised indirectly through DateOfBirthPicker.test.tsx's initial-value-parsing case, but malformed-input edge cases aren't verified against the exported function directly.

`fieldIdByCandidate` (built at lines 95/99, read at line 158) is entirely redundant: `candidateMap.get(resp.fieldId)` only succeeds because `resp.fieldId` is the exact key `fieldIdByCandidate` stores as the value for that candidate, so `fieldIdByCandidate.get(candidate)` always equals `resp.fieldId`. Delete the second Map and use `resp.fieldId` directly as `fieldId`.

`isSkippableOption()` and the inline disabled/empty-value/placeholder-norm checks in `extractSelectOptions()` (src/autofill/ai.ts lines 36-39) duplicate the exact same 'is this a real, fillable <option>' predicate in two files. Extract one shared helper (e.g. next to `PLACEHOLDER_OPTION_NORMS` in normalizer.ts) and use it from both call sites so the two never drift.

All 13 entries in `AUTOCOMPLETE_MAP` hardcode confidence as the bare literal `0.95`, unlike CONF_DICT_EXACT/CONF_CONTEXT/etc., which the project's own convention extracted into constants.ts. Add a `CONF_AUTOCOMPLETE = 0.95` to constants.ts and reference it here instead.

The file header still says the tree is 'shared by the on-page picker overlay (picker.ts)', but picker.ts has already been removed from the codebase. Update the comment so it doesn't point future readers at a deleted file.

`clearHighlights()` re-implements the same three restore/cleanup statements already in `clearElementHighlight()` instead of calling it: `document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('[data-jb-highlighted]').forEach(clearElementHighlight)` would remove the duplication with identical behavior.

`workHistoryHeading` and `educationHeading` are structurally identical (primary/secondary field fallback, then start/end-year range fallback, then 'Entry N') differing only in which two profile fields they read. Could be collapsed into one helper parameterized by primary/secondary field values.

`findBestProfileMatch()` calls `similarity(value, candidate.value)` on raw, un-normalized strings, unlike every other `similarity()` call site in the module (mapper.ts's `dictionaryFuzzy`, filler.ts's `findBestMatch`), which all pass `normalize()`-cased strings first. Because Levenshtein distance is case-sensitive, a user typing a value in different case than the stored profile value can score below `EDIT_LEARN_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` and silently fail to link a learned mapping that should have matched. Normalize both sides before comparing, consistent with the rest of the codebase.

'runAIAutofill — radio fills' and 'runAIAutofill — checkbox fills' only exercise `confidence: 'high'` responses. The `needReview++` / non-green branch for radio and checkbox groups is never hit by a test, even though the equivalent low-confidence path is thoroughly tested for text candidates.

`findBestOption()`'s partial/substring-match fallback is never exercised — all radio/checkbox tests use option labels that match the AI response exactly, plus one 'no match at all' case. A test where the AI returns a substring of a real option label would confirm the fuzzy fallback actually fires.

RE_EMAIL (`/^[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/`) only allows a single dot in the domain, so it rejects valid addresses with multi-level TLDs or subdomains (e.g. user@mail.co.uk, user@company.com.au, user@sub.example.com). Given the extension explicitly targets multi-country job seekers, this will silently reject/flag common real-world emails on profile import. Fix by allowing multiple dot-separated domain labels, e.g. `/^[\w.+-]+@[\w-]+(\.[\w-]+)*\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}$/`.

validateDocumentEntry() checks that file.base64 is a string but never bounds its length, unlike CLAUDE.md's documented 4MB UI cap on CV uploads. An imported/restored profile can carry a CV/cover-letter file well past that cap, which the sanitizer will happily accept and pass through to saveProfile(), risking a chrome.storage.local 5MB quota rejection at write time instead of being caught here with a clear validation error.

In syncProfileToDrive(), the inner try/catch around findBackupFileId() converts any non-DriveApiError into `new DriveApiError(0, '')` before rethrowing, but the outer catch already derives status=0/body='' for any non-DriveApiError error the exact same way. The inner try/catch is dead weight — remove it and let the error propagate to the outer catch unchanged.

DEV_PROFILE.personal.gender is 'Female', veteranStatus is 'Not a veteran', and disabilityStatus is 'No' — none of these match the actual enum values the Personal section dropdowns use ('female'/'male'/'other'/'prefer_not_to_say' and 'yes'/'no'/'prefer_not_to_say'). In `pnpm dev`, these three selects will render blank even though profileCompletion.ts counts them as filled. Fix by using the lowercase enum values.

sessionGet/sessionSet/sessionRemove duplicate the exact try/catch-around-chrome-callback shape of storageGet/storageSet/storageRemove in storage.ts, differing only in which chrome.storage.* area is used and that storage.ts's set rejects on failure while sessionStorage's never does. Consider a small shared factory (e.g. `wrapStorageArea(area, { rejectOnSetError })`) to remove the triplicated boilerplate while preserving the documented behavioral difference.

storageGet/storageSet/storageRemove in storage.ts each have a try/catch around a synchronous throw from chrome.storage.local.*, but storage.test.ts never exercises that path — only the chrome.runtime.lastError callback-based failure is tested. sessionStorage.test.ts has an entire describe block covering the equivalent case for sessionStorage.ts; storage.ts's parallel branches have no such coverage despite being the higher-stakes module.

validateImportedProfile() is a single ~320-line function handling all nine Profile sections inline with repeated typeof/err() boilerplate per field. Extracting one small validator function per section would shrink the function, make each section independently testable/reviewable, and reduce the risk of copy-paste drift between near-identical field checks.

links.linkedin validation only calls err() when the value is a non-empty string that fails the linkedin.com check; if lnk.linkedin is present but not a string at all, neither branch fires and it's silently dropped with no reported error — inconsistent with every other field in this function. Add an `else if (lnk.linkedin !== undefined)` branch that calls err('links.linkedin', ...) for the non-string case.

The comment 'Popular countries pinned first, then all others alphabetically' describes the initial COUNTRIES array literal, but COUNTRIES.sort((a,b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name)) on line 206 immediately re-sorts the whole array purely alphabetically, discarding the pinned ordering. Either drop the sort() (if pinning is actually wanted) or delete the misleading comment/regroup the literal alphabetically to match actual behavior.

The comment above GEMINI_MODEL_PRIORITY ('Must equal GEMINI_MODEL_PRIORITY[0]') is self-referential and doesn't make sense attached to the array's own definition — it appears to be a copy/paste of the comment correctly placed on DEFAULT_GEMINI_MODEL. Remove the stray sentence from the GEMINI_MODEL_PRIORITY comment.

Pages are fetched and scanned for annotations sequentially in a for-loop with `await pdfDoc.getPage(page)` per iteration. Since each page's annotation extraction is independent, this could be parallelized with `Promise.all(...)` to reduce latency on multi-page resumes.

WORK_AUTH_STATUS_LABELS is built with `Object.fromEntries(...) as Record<WorkAuthorizationStatus, string>`, an unchecked cast that gives no compile-time guarantee every WorkAuthorizationStatus member has a label. The accompanying test only checks a circular relationship that can't catch a status added to the union but never added to WORK_AUTH_STATUS_OPTIONS. Replace the cast with an exhaustiveness pattern so a forgotten status fails the build instead of silently missing a label at runtime.

The setValue functions for 'documents.cv.url' and 'documents.cv.file' both repeat the same two-level spread pattern inline rather than sharing a small helper, unlike every other nested field which goes through setNestedField(). Consider a `setDoublyNestedField` helper mirroring setNestedField to remove the duplication.

handleSave awaits saveProfile(synced) with no try/catch, unlike the derivation step just above it and the Drive-sync step just below it. If saveProfile rejects (documented 5MB chrome.storage.local quota limit), the click handler produces an unhandled promise rejection, profile state is never updated, and the user gets zero feedback — no toast, no console.error. Wrap the call in try/catch and surface a toast (mirroring the 'Drive sync failed' warning pattern) on failure.

The 'handleSave contract' describe block covers the derivation-throws path but has no test for saveProfile itself rejecting (e.g. quota exceeded). Add a test asserting user-visible behavior when saveProfile rejects, since this is a real, documented failure mode with currently no error handling in the component.

The 'autofocus first empty input on section navigation' effect calls focusFirstEmpty(document.querySelector('main')) instead of the already-available mainRef.current, which its sibling effect (line 191) correctly uses. Use mainRef.current in both places for consistency and to avoid an extra DOM query.

focusGeminiKey (lines 98-102) and handleFocusField (lines 251-256) both repeat the same three-step pattern (skipAutoFocusRef.current = true; setActiveSection(...); setFocusTarget(...)). Extract a small shared helper, e.g. navigateAndFocus(section, fieldId), to avoid the duplicated sequencing logic.

colorMap is a fully static object (keyed only by the derived `color` string) rebuilt on every render. Hoist the three-entry map to module scope and index into it, since none of its contents depend on props/state.

openDebugPanel — including its multi-frame DebugSession selection logic (picking the session with the highest green+yellow+red+gray total) — has zero test coverage in src/popup/App.test.tsx. Add a test that renders multiple frame sessions via GET_DEBUG_SESSION responses and asserts the one with the most scanned fields is chosen, plus a basic shift-click trigger test.

Only the negative case for the AI nudge is tested (aiAvailable merges true → nudge hidden). There is no test for the positive case: aiAvailable false across all frames, hasGeminiKey false, and nudge not yet dismissed → nudge text should actually render. Add that assertion to close the gap.

The shift+click debug-panel trigger is only reachable via mouse (onClick on an with no role/tabIndex/keydown handler), unlike AiSparkIcon which implements a full keyboard-accessible pattern in the same file's tree. Low-impact since it's a hidden developer feature, but worth a same-file precedent note.

The tooltip only reveals on CSS :hover (peer-hover:opacity-100); the anchor span isn't focusable and there's no peer-focus variant, so keyboard-only and touch users can never see the tooltip text. Add tabIndex={0} to the anchor span and a peer-focus:opacity-100 (or peer-focus-visible:opacity-100) class alongside peer-hover.

The modal backdrop's onClick={onBack} is not guarded by isSaving, while the footer's Back button is explicitly disabled during isSaving. A user can click outside the dialog mid-save and trigger onBack, letting the parent dismiss/unmount the review screen while a save is still in flight. Change to onClick={isSaving ? undefined : onBack} to match the footer's guard.

FieldRow's final branch (rendering a plain label for change.status outside 'new'/'conflict') is dead code: FieldStatus only has 'new' | 'conflict' | 'unchanged', and the only caller always pre-filters to fields.filter(c => c.status !== 'unchanged') before mapping to FieldRow. Remove the unreachable branch or make FieldRow's prop type reflect only 'new' | 'conflict'.

SECTION_ORDER.map re-filters the full `changes` array once per section (9 full scans) to group fields by section, instead of a single pass that buckets changes by section up front. Negligible at typical resume-field volumes, but an easy O(n) improvement if this ever runs on larger change sets.

The CI workflow runs type-check, lint, and build but never runs the Vitest suite (`pnpm test:run`), even though the project has 1000+ unit tests and CLAUDE.md documents `test:run` as required before every commit. A broken test suite can be pushed and merged without CI ever catching it. Add a `pnpm test:run` step after the lint step.

The release workflow only runs `pnpm compile` (type-check) before building, zipping, and uploading to the Chrome Web Store — there is no `pnpm lint` or `pnpm test:run` step. Since pushing a `v*.*.*` tag with a `release` annotation submits directly for CWS review with no CLI rollback, a regression that passes type-check but fails tests/lint can ship to production users. Add lint and test steps before the build/zip step.

The global `keydown` listener fires `fillDemoData()` whenever the 'f' key is pressed anywhere on the page, with no check of `event.target`. If the tester is typing into a text field and types a word containing 'f', it silently overwrites all form fields mid-edit. Guard with a check that `event.target` isn't an input/textarea/select, or require a modifier key.

`.upload-box input { display: none; }` hides the résumé file input using display:none, which removes it from the tab order entirely — keyboard-only users can never reach or activate the file picker via Tab. Use a visually-hidden pattern (e.g. position:absolute; width:1px; height:1px; opacity:0) that keeps the input focusable instead.

All four legal pages (privacy, terms, eula, disclaimer under docs/legal/*/index.html) ship with zero CSS — no stylesheet link, no shared header/nav, no link back to the main site. They render as unstyled black-on-white browser-default text, completely disconnected from the branded landing page a visitor would have just come from. Consider a small shared stylesheet plus a 'back to Job Buddy' link/logo.

The global `ignores` list excludes `docs/**` and `demo-apply-form/**` entirely, so the plain JS files get zero static analysis — not even basic no-undef/syntax checks. Consider adding a minimal JS-only ESLint block scoped to these two files instead of blanket-ignoring them.

`@vitest/coverage-v8` is pinned to an exact version (4.1.9) while `vitest` itself uses a caret range (^4.1.9). These two packages must stay in lockstep; the exact pin can silently drift out of sync the next time `vitest` bumps a minor/patch version via its caret range. Use matching version specifiers for both.

Many fields are marked required via a visual '*' in the label text but none carry the `required` or `aria-required` attribute, so screen readers never announce them as mandatory. Since this is a manual-testing harness it's low-stakes, but adding `required` would make the demo form's accessibility semantics match its visual cues.

handleReset (the 'Reset All Data' flow, gated behind a typed-DELETE confirmation) calls disconnectDrive() and clearAllStorage() — which only removes ['profile','learnedMappings','applicationHistory'] — but never calls clearGeminiSettings() or resets themePreference. The UI copy explicitly promises 'Permanently delete your profile, learned autofill mappings, and all data from this browser. This cannot be undone.' Despite that, the user's Gemini API key and theme preference silently survive a full reset. clearGeminiSettings() already exists and is used elsewhere (invalid-key cleanup) — it is simply not called here.

handleDriveReviewSave (Review -> Apply Selected on a Drive conflict) fired an explicit immediate syncProfileToDrive() on top of the debounced background sync saveProfile() already triggers, double-uploading. Its sibling path handleRestoreFromDrive relied only on the debounced sync.

ApplicationEntry / applicationHistory is a fully modeled, persisted, and exported data type (including a duplicate_warned status implying a duplicate-application-warning feature) that nothing in the autofill flow ever writes to. Only ever round-trips through export/import in SettingsSection. Needs a product decision: build the feature or remove the dead scaffolding.

AUTOFILL_SCAN and AUTOFILL_FILL message handlers catch and silently discard the underlying error before falling back to an empty response, with no console.error — every other error path in the codebase logs before falling back. A real scan/fill crash currently produces zero diagnostic trail.

handleImportComplete's catch only console.errors, no showToast — unlike handleSave's catch (line 250-253) which does. If getProfile() throws after an import/reset/Drive-restore completes, the user sees no feedback and the UI sits in stale pre-reset state, even though the underlying write already succeeded (only the reload failed).

ImportSummaryDialog and ImportReviewScreen are sibling dialogs used back-to-back in the same flows (Resume Import, Drive conflict resolution) but handle dismissal inconsistently: ImportReviewScreen supports Escape and backdrop-click; ImportSummaryDialog supports neither.

documents.coverLetter is a real, validated profile field with live UI, but has no FIELD_DEFS entry in parser.ts. generateDiff/applyChanges (shared by Resume Import, Import Profile, and Drive Connect) only ever write fields present in FIELD_DEFS, so an imported JSON export or Drive backup containing a coverLetter is silently dropped even under Accept All. Real data-loss risk.

Same root cause as f-0230: buildPickerTree()'s Documents section only emits a row for documents.cv.url. documents.coverLetter has no row, so a user with a saved cover letter can never select it as a Learned Mapping target.
Zero test coverage of the Documents section for coverLetter in either buildPickerTree() or FIELD_DEFS setValue — add cases once f-0230/f-0231 are fixed.

checkApiKey() calls encodeURIComponent(apiKey) when building its request URL; the shared endpoint() helper used by validateApiKey/extractFromResume/resolveFieldsWithAI does not. Inconsistent treatment of the same value.

useDropdownPanel.ts duplicates open-state/search/outside-click/focus-on-open plumbing already in useSearchableDropdown.ts — nearly identical logic, only the filter/highlight machinery differs. Extract a smaller shared primitive both hooks compose from.

DateOfBirthPicker.tsx and MonthYearPicker.tsx each implement the identical resync-when-value-changes-during-render pattern (~10-line prevValue block). Extract a shared useResyncOnExternalChange(value, onResync) hook.

The 'salary.expected' dictionary marker resolves via resolveDictionaryHit() to the literal path salary.expected, but resolveProfileValue() has no case for that bare path and falls through to generic traversal, which returns '' for any array value. Unlike languages/education/workHistory (each with a dedicated adjustXMatches() sibling-resolution pass rewriting the marker to prefix.N.field), salary never got the same treatment — no salaryResolution.ts exists. Any field exact-matching this dictionary entry always resolves empty and lands in gray/noData, never actually autofilling expected salary.

findBestOption (AI-selected radio/checkbox matching) uses naive case-insensitive substring inclusion with no similarity threshold, meaningfully looser than findBestMatch in filler.ts (Levenshtein similarity, threshold-gated) used for the rule-pipeline's own select/ARIA-listbox matching. A short generic option label could substring-match an unrelated longer one.

The 'derived.totalExperience.years' switch case is functionally identical to what the generic dot-notation traversal at the bottom of the same function already produces for any numeric leaf. Dead/redundant special case.
scanned.map((s) => s.match) is called 4 separate times in a row (once per sibling-resolution pass), each allocating a new array over identical data. Hoist to one const and reuse.

Module-level fuzzyCache Map is never cleared. Content scripts persist across SPA client-side navigation, so on a job site with many route changes this cache grows unboundedly for the tab's lifetime. Likely low real-world impact but worth a decision on capping/clearing.

Live per-field validation duplicates save-time validate() logic independently in 5 section files, risking drift. Already drifted once: PersonalSection's live fieldError has no max-length check for firstName/lastName even though validate() does (nickname correctly has both). SalarySection's expectedRowErrors() and WorkHistorySection's validateNoticePeriod() already prove the fix pattern elsewhere in this codebase — a single validator called from both the live handler and validate().
Sidebar.tsx hand-rolls MenuIcon/GearIcon inline SVG components while the same file already imports FileUp/Brain from lucide-react. lucide-react's Menu/Settings icons can likely replace both.
The Required Fields and Optional Fields dropdown-trigger blocks are near-identical JSX differing only in count/heading/groups/bulletCls. Extract one shared sub-component taking those as props.
The identical custom-link URL-validity check is triplicated verbatim in updateCustom, handleCustomUrlBlur, and validate(). Extract one helper.

ethnicity field validation is inconsistent with its siblings (gender, veteranStatus, disabilityStatus) — those check against a VALID_* allowlist and report an error on failure; ethnicity only checks typeof === 'string' with no length cap and no error on invalid type. The UI always renders a fixed ETHNICITIES select, but an imported/restored profile could carry a garbage value that silently passes validation.

getDriveToken/saveDriveToken/clearDriveToken, getDriveBackupState/saveDriveBackupState, getThemePreference/saveThemePreference are structurally identical get/set/clear boilerplate around storageGet/storageSet. Could share a generic accessor factory.

retryPendingDriveSync() and syncIfConnected() are ~70% duplicated (fetch token+profile, guard, call syncProfileToDrive, silent catch), differing only in whether they also check state.pendingSync. Could share a helper.
withScheme() has no dedicated unit test, only indirectly exercised via migrate.test.ts. Its own doc comment calls out a documented edge case (empty-string input) not directly locked in by a test.

queryAllDeep() performs a full querySelectorAll('*') walk of the DOM (recursing into open shadow roots) purely to discover shadow hosts, invoked independently by scanFields, scanRadioGroups, scanCheckboxGroups, and 4 separate selectors inside scanAriaFields — up to 7 full-page traversals per scan cycle redoing the same shadow-root discovery. Consolidating into one shadow-root-aware walk would cut this to one traversal; flagged needs-review since it touches the shared low-level scan primitive.
EXCLUDED_INPUT_TYPES includes 'image' and 'reset', but scanner.test.ts only tests exclusion for hidden/submit/button/checkbox/radio/file. Minor gap, same pattern as the tested ones.

isSkippableOption has zero test coverage — normalizer.test.ts only covers normalize/similarity. This function is explicitly shared between filler.ts's fillSelect and ai.ts's extractSelectOptions 'so the two never drift' per its own comment, making it a correctness-critical, cross-file-relied-upon helper with no direct test locking in its behavior.
